item: Row 360: the release-notes generator's tests build their own two-release history
summary: Three tests (the CLI end to end, commit_day under three timezones, previous_tag's twin) read v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 from the runner's clone. CI checks out at depth 1, so they passed only when the script's own unshallow reached the network (red on #2302, green on main the same day). They now build a non-shallow repo with no remote whose first-parent history carries both tags at the real committer dates, identity and dates through the environment with no git config written, and point the shipped script's git at it; the ledger, consent test and gate file are still the real tree's. Shown: in a shallow clone with no remote the old tests fail and the new pass; breaking previous_tag or commit_day still fails them. The SHALLOW refusal and its tests are unchanged.
